summary: Specific notice periods apply depending on how long you've been renting and who is terminating the tenancy.
explanation: The notice period depends on how long you've been renting. For tenancies of less than 6 months, 28 days' notice is required. For 6 months to 1 year, 35 days. For 1-2 years, 42 days. For 2-3 years, 56 days. For 3-4 years, 84 days. For 4-5 years, 112 days. For 5+ years, 140 days.
compliant_examples: Termination requires notice periods as specified by the Residential Tenancies Act
Notice periods will be in accordance with current legislation
Landlord will provide legally required notice periods based on tenancy duration
non_compliant_examples: Landlord may terminate with 14 days' notice regardless of tenancy duration
Tenant must vacate within one week if requested
Landlord reserves the right to shorten notice periods
recommended_action: If your lease contains incorrect notice periods, inform your landlord that these clauses are unenforceable. The statutory notice periods in the Residential Tenancies Act apply regardless of what's in the lease.

summary: Landlords must still give proper notice for entry during the notice period.
explanation: Even after a notice of termination has been served, your landlord must still give you reasonable notice (typically 24 hours) before entering the property for viewings or inspections.
alert_if_found: landlord may enter at any time after notice
no notice required for entry after termination notice
compliant_examples: Landlord will give 24 hours' notice for viewings during notice period
Reasonable notice required for all access during notice period
non_compliant_examples: Landlord may enter at any time for viewings once notice is served
Tenant must allow access for viewings without further notice
Unrestricted access for showing property to prospective tenants
recommended_action: If your lease allows unlimited access during the notice period, inform your landlord that they must still provide reasonable notice (typically 24 hours) before entering for viewings or inspections.

summary: Tenants must continue to pay rent and follow the lease terms during the notice period.
explanation: During the notice period, you must continue to pay rent and comply with all terms of your lease until the termination date. Failure to do so could result in loss of deposit or other penalties.
alert_if_found: deposit serves as last month's rent
tenant may leave early without penalty
compliant_examples: Tenant must continue to pay rent until the termination date
All lease terms remain in effect during notice period
Rent and utilities must be paid in full until move-out date
non_compliant_examples: Deposit will be used as final month's rent
Tenant may cease paying rent once notice is given
Lease terms end when notice is served
recommended_action: Continue paying rent and following all lease terms until the termination date. Keep records of all payments and communications during the notice period.

summary: Landlords can only end a tenancy after 6 months for specific legal reasons.
explanation: After the first 6 months of a tenancy, a landlord can only end the tenancy for specific reasons, such as selling the property, needing it for their own use, significant renovation, change of use, or breach of tenant obligations.
compliant_examples: Landlord may terminate for reasons specified in the Residential Tenancies Act
Termination requires valid grounds after 6 months of tenancy
Notice must state the specific legal ground for termination
non_compliant_examples: Landlord reserves the right to terminate at any time without reason
Tenancy may be ended at landlord's sole discretion
Landlord may terminate without specifying grounds
recommended_action: If your landlord tries to end your tenancy without specifying a valid legal ground, challenge the notice through the RTB dispute resolution process. A termination notice without a valid ground is not legally enforceable after 6 months of tenancy.
